summary: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Sorbonne University, the Old Catholic Seminary of Amersfoort, and under Darab Kumana, later serving as an oriental language interpreter and academy member.

Abraham Sachs was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1934–1937). He was affiliated with the Institute for Advanced Study in 1945 and held a post at Brown University (~1948–1983).
Abraham Zablocki works in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Cornell University and held a post at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).
Acharya Buddharakkhita studied under U Nārada and Mahasi Sayadaw (~1952–1954). He later taught Laurence Khantipalo Mills.

Achim Bayer is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his MA under David P. Jackson and his PhD from the University of Hamburg (2005) under Lambert Schmithausen. He was a research associate at the University of Munich (2004–2006).

Adalbert Bezzenberger was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen and at Munich. After habilitating at Göttingen, he became Professor of Sanskrit at Königsberg in 1879, where he later served as prorector and rector.

Adalbert Kuhn was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin. He worked at the Köllnisches Gymnasium from 1837 as teacher, professor, and director, and was a member of the Prussian Academy.

Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Greg Bailey and served as a senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).
Adam Hardy works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Trinity College, Cambridge, he served as Professor of Asian Architecture at Cardiff University (~2005) and directed PRASADA.

Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, while also studying under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers.

Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Erlangen-Nürnberg, Bonn, and Marburg, she served as a visiting professor at the University of Vienna (~2005) and as Privatdozentin at the University of Marburg (2009).

Adelheid Mette was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She held professorships at the University of Munich before serving as Indology chair at the University of Münster (1988–2000).

Aden Kumler is an art historian who studied at Chicago, Toronto, Harvard (PhD), and the Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies. She held faculty posts at the University of Chicago (2007–2020) before becoming professor at the University of Basel in 2020.
Adeu Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Samten Gyatso and Drukpa Choegon Rinpoche, and he later taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.
Adi Da worked in religious studies and philosophy. He completed his studies at Columbia University (~1957–1961) and Stanford University (~1961–1963).

Adinath Neminath Upadhye was an Indologist who earned his BA and D.Litt. from the University of Mumbai. He taught Prakrit at Rajaram College (1930–1962), served as Professor Emeritus at Shivaji University, and chaired Jaina studies at Mysore (1971).

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bopp, Schlegel, Lassen, and others in Berlin, Bonn, and Paris. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and librarian at the University of Breslau from 1833 to 1872.

Adolf Holtzmann was an Indologist and linguist. He studied in Berlin, Halle, Munich (under Othmar Frank and Johann Andreas Schmeller), and Paris (under Eugène Burnouf), later serving as Professor of German Literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University (1852–1870).

Adolf Kaegi was a Swiss Indologist and linguist. Educated at Zurich, Tübingen (under Rudolf von Roth), and Leipzig, he spent his career at the University of Zurich, becoming Ordinary Professor of Sanskrit, Indo-European, and Classical Philology (1893–1914).

Adolf Kießling was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology who studied under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1856–1858). He held academic posts at the University of Basel (~1869–1877), Greifswald (~1877–1889), and Göttingen (~1889–1893).
